name: Prediction Radar — following top-graded directional Polymarket sports wallets at the price 5 minutes later
registered_before: any Polymarket response was read for this study: Polymarket's hosts are refused by the build environment's network policy, so no leaderboard, trade, holder, market or price was seen before this file was committed. The runner (research/radar/run_validation.js) refuses to run if this file has changed since registration.
hypothesis: Positions that top-graded directional wallets enter on EdgeDesk-covered games, followed at the price 5 minutes later, beat the closing price more than 50% of the time and have positive follow ROI.
objective: Measure, once, on a holdout window chosen before any data was read, whether a follower who copies the pregame positions of the 25 highest Radar-Score directional Polymarket sports wallets (graded only on their earlier history) at the market price 5 minutes after each entry beats the closing price more than half the time and makes money holding to settlement. Report what the test finds, good or bad: the Prediction Radar record section quotes it verbatim. Research only: no wallet, side or price is a recommendation.
primary_metric: Two, both required: (a) the beat-close rate of followed bets, beat = the closing price is strictly above the follow price; (b) the mean follow ROI per followed bet, follow ROI = settlement / follow price - 1 (one unit staked per bet, held to settlement). Each with its game-clustered 95% bootstrap interval.
unit: One followed bet: one selected wallet's pregame position in one outcome of one covered market (its first pregame BUY of that outcome token), followed once at the price 5 minutes after that first BUY. Two wallets on the same side of the same market are two bets. Clusters: the game (the Polymarket event).
baseline: A follower who buys at a random moment pays the market price and, with no information, beats the close half the time at best (the price is a martingale under its own measure) and loses the spread and any fee: a beat-close rate of 50% and a follow ROI of 0 (before costs) is the no-skill line. The wallets' own entry prices are not available to a follower; the test measures only what a follower could get.
training_window: Grading only (nothing is fitted): each pool wallet is graded on its bets on covered games that started in [2025-09-01, 2026-09-01) UTC, using at most its 150 most recent graded bets in that window.
validation_window: None. Nothing is tuned; every threshold below is fixed in advance.
holdout_window: Bets of the selected wallets whose first pregame BUY and whose game start are both in [2026-09-01, 2026-10-26) UTC. Looked at once.

minimum_sample.note: Below 200 followed bets with a follow price, a close and a settlement in the holdout, the result is descriptive and H-RADAR-01 cannot pass. Every followed bet counts, losses included.

promotion_criteria.decision_rule: passed = true only if ALL THREE criteria hold on the holdout. A criterion that cannot be evaluated is not met. Passing makes Prediction Radar eligible to drop its Experimental label; it does not drop it: a person does that through a validation report. Software tests passing is never evidence for any criterion. The point estimates in the hypothesis (above 50%, above zero) are reported beside the criteria but do not by themselves pass the test.

criteria.rule: At least 200 followed bets in the holdout with a follow price, a close and a settlement of 0, 0.5 or 1.
The lower end of the two-sided 95% percentile interval of the beat-close rate is above 0.50.
The lower end of the two-sided 95% percentile interval of the mean follow ROI (5 minutes) is above zero.

promotion_criteria.interval: A cluster bootstrap that resamples whole games (Polymarket events) with replacement: 2,000 resamples, mulberry32 seeded 20261029 (lib/edgedesk_radar.js clusterBootstrap), because bets on one game share its news, its close and its result.
promotion_criteria.family_correction: All three are required (an intersection test); none is reported as a pass on its own.

candidates_tried.pool: Polymarket sports leaderboard, all time, ordered by volume, top 200
candidates_tried.selection: Directional, at least 50 graded bets, history not truncated, top 25 by Radar Score
candidates_tried.radar_score: 100 x (0.5 follow ROI + 0.3 CLV% + 0.2 ROI), each shrunk by n / (n + 50)
candidates_tried.close: last price at or before the game start, at most 60 minutes before it

alternatives_considered_not_tried: a pool ordered by profit instead of volume (it would select on the outcomes it is meant to predict)
the top 10 or the top 50 wallets instead of 25
the ask instead of the recorded market price (reported as a +1 cent sensitivity, never used for the verdict)
weighting a followed bet by the wallet's stake
other Radar Score weights, or ranking on follow ROI alone
player props, futures and non-game markets
forking_paths.choice_and_reason: One candidate, written before any data: volume ordering to keep the pool from being chosen on results; 25 wallets, the number Smart Money Tonight counts as top-graded, so the test measures the population the product shows; 5 minutes, the owner's follow definition; the market price, the owner's follow definition, with a +1 cent sensitivity because a follower pays at least the spread; one unit per bet, so a few large stakes cannot carry the result.
forking_paths.data_already_seen: None. No Polymarket response had been read by the author when this file was committed (the hosts are blocked in the build environment). The pool is drawn when the runner runs, from the leaderboard as it stands that day, so it can include wallets whose volume or survival owes something to the holdout window: disclosed in known_limitations.
secondary_reported_not_tested: follow ROI and beat-close rate at 15 minutes
follow ROI with the follow price raised by 1 cent
the selected wallets' own ROI and CLV in the holdout
the same metrics for all ranked directional wallets, not only the top 25
forking_paths.stopping_rule: One look. The runner refuses to fetch while a completed report for this version exists; a second look needs a new registered version that counts this one.

spec.covered_games: Historical test: a Polymarket market is on an EdgeDesk-covered game when Polymarket files its event under a league EdgeDesk's board covers (NFL, college football, NBA, NHL, MLB), the market is a game market of type moneyline, spreads or totals, and it carries a game start time. The board's historical event list is not in this repository, so coverage is defined by league here; the live product matches each market to one EdgeDesk game (signals.event_id).
spec.pool_fallback: If the leaderboard cannot be ordered by volume, the all-time profit ordering is used and the report says so in its first line.
spec.bet: A wallet's position in one outcome token of a covered market whose first BUY came before the game start. Entry time: that first BUY. Entry price: the volume-weighted price of its BUYs before the start. Stake: the cost of those BUYs. Graded once the market resolved with each outcome settling at 0, 0.5 or 1; otherwise void and excluded.

wallet_grade.record: wins (settlement 1), losses (0), pushes (0.5) of the outcome held
wallet_grade.profit: sell proceeds + settlement x shares still held - buy cost, over every trade on the token (pregame and in-play): the money the wallet actually made
wallet_grade.clv: close - entry price (probability points) and close / entry - 1 (CLV%, the house formula: entry decimal x closing fair - 1), averaged over bets with a close
wallet_grade.follow_roi: settlement / follow price - 1, follow price = the last recorded price at or before entry + 5 minutes (also 15), no older than 10 minutes, and only if entry + lag is before the start; averaged over bets with a follow price
wallet_grade.conviction: a bet's stake / the wallet's median graded stake; 3x or more is high conviction
wallet_grade.style: Market Maker: at least half of its covered markets two-sided (both outcomes bought), a median of 6 or more trades per market and a median net ratio |shares A - shares B| / (shares A + shares B) of 0.3 or less. Hedger: not a market maker, and at least 20% of markets two-sided. Directional: everything else. Market makers are never selected.
wallet_grade.sample: graded bets (at most the 150 most recent); fewer than 50 is a small sample with no rank and no Radar Score
wallet_grade.radar_score: EXPERIMENTAL composite, ranked wallets only: 100 x (0.5 s(follow ROI) + 0.3 s(CLV%) + 0.2 s(ROI)), s(x) = x x m / (m + 50) where m is the number of bets that component is measured on; always shown with its components

spec.prices: Polymarket CLOB price history (prices-history, 1-minute fidelity) of the outcome token; the recorded price, not the ask.
spec.data_access: Polymarket's public Data API (leaderboard, activity), Gamma API (markets) and CLOB price history, read through the Radar gateway (lib/edgedesk_poly_gateway.js) with its request budget and backoff, from a GitHub Actions runner (.github/workflows/radar-validation.yml) because the build environment cannot reach Polymarket. Everything read is kept as the run's artifact, and its sha256 is in the report.
spec.code: lib/edgedesk_radar.js (grading, follow, close, bootstrap), lib/edgedesk_poly_gateway.js (every request), research/radar/run_validation.js (the protocol)
known_limitations: Polymarket's public data is its international platform; a US reader may not be able to trade the same markets
a follower never gets the wallet's entry price; the recorded price is not the ask, and fees are not modelled
the pool is drawn from today's leaderboard, so it can favour wallets that survived or grew through the holdout
wallets whose history exceeds 30 pages of activity are excluded (counted), which removes some of the busiest traders
covered games are defined by league in this historical test, not by EdgeDesk's own event list
past results do not predict future results, and some large traders may have information others do not
